high.title: Dollar-Won Retreats from Highs as Warsh Eases Inflation Concerns – Closes at 1,551.20 Won
high.summary: The USD/KRW rate pulled back during overnight New York trading, closing at 1,551.20 won at 2:00 AM KST on July 2nd — up just 1.80 won from the previous Seoul session close, but notably down 3.70 won from the day session close of 1,554.90 won. The retreat appears to have been triggered by comments from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh that helped alleviate near-term inflation concerns, weighing on the dollar broadly. The intraday reversal is meaningful: the pair had been testing the upper 1,550s during the New York session before sellers stepped in. For KRW traders, the key question is whether this pullback represents a sustainable USD softening or merely a technical correction within a broader dollar-supportive environment. The 1,550 psychological level remains a critical pivot. If U.S. inflation rhetoric stays contained and risk appetite improves, KRW could see modest appreciation pressure. However, with the won still trading above 1,550, underlying structural demand for the dollar remains intact. Watch for Seoul's opening fix and any BOK intervention signals near resistance.

high.title: Dollar-Won Trades in Upper 1,550s in New York Session
high.summary: The USD/KRW rate surged to 1,557.70 won as of 9:28 PM KST on July 1st during the New York session, representing an 8.10 won rise from the prior session — a significant intraday move suggesting broad-based dollar strength and/or KRW selling pressure. The regular Seoul session had already closed higher at 1,554.90 won (+5.50 won), meaning offshore momentum continued to push the pair further above that level. This back-to-back upward trajectory in USD/KRW is a clear warning signal for KRW bulls. A sustained break above the 1,555–1,560 band could open the door to further topside risk. Fund managers should monitor whether BOK smoothing operations materialize at these elevated levels, and track U.S. macro data (particularly jobs and inflation) that could anchor or extend dollar strength heading into the July FOMC window.

high.title: Dollar-Won Falls Below Expectations on Weak US Jobs Data, Closes at 1,540.00 Won
high.summary:
The dollar-won exchange rate dropped sharply in New York overnight trading, closing at 1,540.00 won — a decline of 14.90 won from the previous Seoul FX market close. The catalyst was US nonfarm payrolls data coming in below market expectations, which materially reduced the probability of a Federal Reserve rate hike and triggered a broad dollar-weakening, won-strengthening dynamic. This is a significant move for KRW traders: a sub-1,540 close in New York suggests the Seoul open on July 3rd will be under meaningful downward pressure on USD/KRW. For bond investors, a stronger won combined with receding Fed hike expectations could support Korean government bond (KTB) prices, as it reduces imported inflation pressures and gives the Bank of Korea more policy flexibility. FX managers should monitor whether this move sustains through the Seoul session or faces profit-taking. Key levels to watch: 1,535 support and whether the 1,540 level becomes resistance on any dollar bounce.

---

medium.title: BOK Governor Shin Hyun-song: CBDCs and Stablecoins Can Coexist
medium.summary: Bank of Korea Governor Shin Hyun-song, speaking at the ECB's Sintra Forum in Portugal, affirmed that central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) and stablecoins can coexist within the financial system, even under crisis conditions. While the article is truncated, the Governor's public stance at a major global central banking forum carries moderate relevance for KRW and monetary policy watchers. The BOK's evolving position on digital currencies could influence future payment infrastructure, reserve management frameworks, and capital flow dynamics. Investors should monitor whether the BOK accelerates its CBDC pilot program, as broader adoption could affect interbank settlement efficiency and have downstream implications for KRW liquidity conditions.

medium.title: BOK Governor: Korea Two Years Ahead of Europe in Monetary Tokenization
medium.summary: Governor Shin Hyun-song presented findings from "Project Hangang" — Korea's unified ledger initiative — at the ECB Forum, claiming Korea leads Europe by approximately two years in monetary tokenization implementation. Critically, the Governor flagged that tokenization of **government bonds** could enable more precise monetary policy execution and support financial stability, a statement directly relevant to Korean government bond (KTB) market structure. If KTBs move toward tokenized issuance or settlement, this could reshape liquidity dynamics, foreign investor access, and yield formation. Bond market participants should track BOK communications on Project Hangang timelines and any regulatory frameworks that may follow from this international signaling.

medium.title: US June Manufacturing PMI Maintains Expansion, Falls Short of All Estimates (Full Report)
medium.summary: U.S. manufacturing activity remained in expansion territory in June, with the ISM PMI printing at 53.3 (down 0.7 points from May's 54.0) and the S&P Global PMI at 53.9 — both coming in below consensus estimates. While still expansionary, the deceleration suggests that U.S. economic momentum may be moderating, which carries mixed implications for EM currencies including the KRW. A softer U.S. growth trajectory could temper Fed hawkishness and reduce upward pressure on USD/KRW, though the miss-versus-expectations dynamic could also fuel risk-off sentiment temporarily. Korean equity and FX traders should watch whether this data feeds into broader dollar retreat narratives or is offset by resilient U.S. labor market prints later this week.

medium.title: Warsh Appoints Former BOE Governor Mervyn King as Co-Chair of Communications Task Force
medium.summary: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh has appointed former Bank of England Governor Mervyn King as co-chair of a newly formed Fed communications task force, reflecting an accelerating push to reform how the Federal Reserve communicates policy. While primarily a structural/institutional story, this development is worth monitoring for KRW and Korean bond investors as any shift in Fed communication strategy could alter how markets price U.S. rate expectations — a key driver of USD/KRW direction. A more hawkish or opaque Fed communication style could add volatility to EM FX, while a more transparent approach may help anchor rate expectations. The longer-term implications for global risk appetite and dollar dynamics remain to be seen.

medium.title: Fed's Waller Affirms Central Bank Independence, Cites Supreme Court Ruling on Governor Cook
medium.summary: Speaking at the ECB Forum in Sintra, Portugal, Fed Governor Christopher Waller reaffirmed the Federal Reserve's commitment to institutional independence following the Supreme Court's decision to block President Trump's attempt to remove Governor Lisa Cook. Waller emphasized that the Fed was already acting independently prior to the ruling and remains guided solely by its dual mandate. For KRW and Korean rates markets, sustained Fed independence reduces the tail risk of politicized U.S. monetary policy, which would otherwise inject significant volatility into EM FX and global bond markets. Markets have been sensitive to any erosion of Fed credibility; Waller's comments are modestly stabilizing for risk sentiment.

medium.title: KOSPI Falls Over 2% on Foreign Selling and Pension Rebalancing Concerns
medium.summary:
Foreign selling pressure drove the KOSPI down more than 2%, with large-cap semiconductor stocks bearing the brunt of profit-taking despite South Korea recording a historic monthly export figure surpassing $100 billion for the first time. Pension fund rebalancing concerns amplified the downside. Notably, capital rotated rapidly into KOSDAQ small and mid-cap materials, parts, and equipment stocks, pushing that index higher. For KRW traders, the sustained foreign equity outflows are worth monitoring closely — persistent foreign selling on the KOSPI can translate into USD demand and KRW depreciation pressure, particularly if repatriation of equity proceeds accelerates. The record export data, while a positive signal for the trade balance and a potential KRW support factor in the medium term, was insufficient to offset near-term selling dynamics. Watch for continued foreign net selling data and any BOK commentary on FX stability.

---

medium.title: OECD Urges South Korea to Shift Property Tax from Transactions to Holdings
medium.summary: The OECD has issued a recommendation for South Korea to gradually restructure its property tax regime — moving away from transaction-based levies toward holding-based taxation, with higher rates targeted at vacant homes and second properties. Notably, the OECD also addressed monetary policy, urging the Bank of Korea to maintain a focus on anchoring long-term inflation expectations and to prepare for potential tightening. This monetary policy commentary is of direct relevance to KRW and Korean government bond (KTB) traders: any signal that the BOK may be nudged toward a less accommodative stance could steepen the yield curve and provide modest KRW support. Investors should monitor whether the BOK formally responds to this OECD guidance ahead of upcoming rate decisions, as it could influence forward rate expectations and bond positioning.

medium.title: Meta's AI Pivot Triggers Global Chip Sell-Off, Sending Kospi Below 8,000
medium.summary: South Korea's Kospi index suffered a dramatic decline of nearly 10%, falling below the 8,000 level amid a global semiconductor sell-off triggered by Meta's AI strategy shift. For KRW and capital flow watchers, a move of this magnitude in Korean equities typically generates meaningful foreign equity outflows, which would exert depreciation pressure on the KRW/USD exchange rate. The scale of the sell-off — combined with the broader risk-off sentiment in global chip stocks — warrants close monitoring of BOK FX intervention signals and any widening of the USD/KRW spot rate. Korean government bond yields may also see safe-haven inflows domestically, potentially flattening the short end of the KTB curve.

medium.title: Dollar-Won Trades in Late 1,540s in New York Session
medium.summary: Earlier in the New York session, before the full impact of the jobs data was absorbed, the dollar-won rate stood at 1,548.40 won as of 9:06 PM KST — down 6.50 won from the prior session. This article captures the intraday trajectory that preceded the sharper decline to 1,540.00 won reported later, illustrating that KRW appreciation accelerated significantly as US employment data filtered through markets. The sequential move from ~1,548 to 1,540 within the same session underscores the sensitivity of USD/KRW to US macro data surprises and Fed rate expectations. KRW traders should note the velocity of the move as a risk management consideration heading into the Seoul open.

medium.title: US Treasuries Mixed as Tepid Jobs Data Dampens Rate Hike Bets
medium.summary: US Treasury markets showed mixed price action following the weaker-than-expected nonfarm payrolls print. The 10-year Treasury yield edged marginally higher to 4.477% (+0.20 bps), while shorter-dated yields declined as rate hike bets faded — a classic bull-flattening signal in the front end. For Korean bond investors, a relatively anchored 10-year UST yield at 4.477% limits the upward pull on KTB yields from the US side, while reduced Fed hike expectations are broadly supportive of EM fixed income including KTBs. Watch whether the UST 10-year can sustain below 4.50%, as a break above that level could renew pressure on Korean long-end yields and capital flow dynamics.

medium.title: San Francisco Fed President Says Monetary Policy 'Slightly Restrictive' but Next Move Uncertain
medium.summary: San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly characterized current US monetary policy as "slightly restrictive" while explicitly acknowledging that the Fed's next move remains uncertain, citing robust AI-related investment as a complicating factor. This cautious, data-dependent tone from a Fed official aligns with the market's reaction to the weak jobs print — reducing near-term rate hike probability without fully endorsing a cut cycle. For KRW and KTB markets, prolonged Fed uncertainty at restrictive-but-stable rates means the interest rate differential with Korea remains a key driver of capital flows. A Fed on hold with downside data risks is modestly supportive of KRW stability, but removes a clear catalyst for sustained won appreciation.

medium.title: US Weekly Jobless Claims Fall to 215,000, Below Expectations
medium.summary: US initial jobless claims declined week-over-week to 215,000, printing below consensus expectations. For KRW/USD traders, a resilient US labor market reduces the near-term probability of Fed rate cuts, reinforcing USD strength and maintaining upward pressure on the USD/KRW exchange rate. This dynamic is particularly relevant for the Bank of Korea, which must balance domestic growth concerns against a widening Korea-US rate differential that could accelerate capital outflows and further weaken the Won. Bond investors should note that a strong US labor backdrop keeps UST yields elevated, which in turn pressures Korean government bond (KTB) yields higher via global rate transmission. Watch the upcoming US nonfarm payrolls print (also referenced in Article 2 as coming in weak) for a potentially conflicting signal — the interplay between claims data and payrolls will be critical in shaping Fed expectations and, by extension, the KRW and KTB outlook into Q3 2026.

medium.title: New York Stocks Open Higher as Markets Digest Weak Jobs Report
medium.summary: US equities opened broadly higher following a weaker-than-expected nonfarm payrolls report, with the Dow (+0.47%), S&P 500 (+0.35%), and Nasdaq (+0.20%) all advancing. The soft payrolls data revived market expectations for Fed rate cuts, which is marginally KRW-supportive as it could narrow the Korea-US rate differential and ease pressure on USD/KRW. For Korean equity investors, a risk-on US session typically provides a positive overnight lead for the KOSPI open. However, the divergence between weak payrolls and strong jobless claims (Article 1) introduces uncertainty around the durability of any Fed dovish pivot narrative — a key variable to monitor heading into the next FOMC meeting.

medium.title: Samsung Securities Bond Offering Draws KRW 1.9 Trillion in Orders, KRW 1 Trillion for 3-Year Notes
medium.summary:
Samsung Securities (rated AA+) successfully priced a KRW 300 billion corporate bond offering, attracting KRW 1.87 trillion in total orders — approximately **6.2x oversubscribed** — signaling robust domestic demand for high-grade Korean credit. The 2-year tranche (KRW 100 billion target) drew KRW 580 billion in orders, while the 3-year tranche (KRW 150 billion target) attracted approximately KRW 1 trillion. The strong oversubscription ratio is a meaningful secondary signal for Korean fixed income markets, suggesting domestic institutional investors remain willing to deploy capital into investment-grade corporate paper, which in turn reflects underlying confidence in the rates environment. For KRW bond investors, this level of demand at the corporate credit level may provide modest support for Korean government bond (KTB) sentiment as well, indicating that duration appetite has not meaningfully deteriorated. Traders should monitor whether this demand is driven by rate expectations (anticipating a BOK cut cycle) or simply liquidity deployment, as the distinction has different implications for KTB yields.
